title: A strong converse for stabilizer codes over Pauli channels via the blowing-up lemma
abstract: We prove a strong converse for quantum communication over Pauli channels within the class of stabilizer codes. If a code whose code space is a full joint eigenspace of a stabilizer group transmits above the coherent information of its own input state, its entanglement fidelity decays exponentially in the block length; the encoder may be any isometry onto that space and the decoder any channel. For memoryless channels this determines the $\varepsilon$-quantum capacity of the class for every $\varepsilon < 1$, so that tolerating a constant error buys no rate; for antidegradable channels, such as the depolarizing channel with error probability $p \in [1/4, 3/4]$, that capacity is zero, while for $p \in [1/4,1/2)$ partial-transposition bounds provably cannot certify a strong converse. The proof uses neither additivity assumptions nor semidefinite relaxations: optimal decoding succeeds precisely on an event in a product probability space, so the blowing-up lemma of Ahlswede, Gács and Körner applies, and the side information it produces is charged against the coherent information. The argument also constrains near-deterministic decoding for codes of any kind, and we isolate the encoder-side statement that would extend it to all of them.
summary: This work proves a strong converse for the quantum capacity of stabilizer codes under Pauli noise. By leveraging the blowing-up lemma and avoiding common mathematical assumptions, it rigorously shows that exceeding the coherent information rate leads to exponentially decaying fidelity. This advances fundamental understanding of error correction limits in quantum communication.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove a strong converse for quantum communication capacity when using stabilizer codes over Pauli noise channels.
main_result: It establishes that if the transmission rate exceeds the coherent information, the entanglement fidelity must decay exponentially with block length, providing a strong bound on achievable rates.
method: The proof employs the blowing-up lemma from classical probability theory and reduces the quantum problem to an entropic accounting argument involving side information derived from decoding success events.
model_or_system: The system models quantum communication using stabilizer codes subjected to memoryless Pauli channels, analyzed asymptotically over large block lengths (n).
key_observables: Entanglement Fidelity ($F$), Coherent Information ($	ext{Ic}$), and the rate of information transmission.
important_parameters: Pauli error probability ($p$) for the depolarizing channel; the exponent $\gamma$ defining the excess rate over capacity.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on the structure of stabilizer codes and crucially excludes the possibility of two-way classical assistance.

paper_structure: The paper develops the converse by first relating optimal fidelity to measure theory via the blowing-up lemma, then using side information derived from decoding success events to constrain the achievable rate through an entropic bound.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous, non-asymptotic bounds on quantum channel capacity that do not rely on standard assumptions like additivity or semidefinite programming, which are foundational tools in open quantum systems theory.
